reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes copy trading by highlighting the speaker's approximate 11 percent weekly earnings and directing viewers to a description link to get started. The description advertises a crypto-trading bonus, while related pages present exceptionally large return figures and describe copy trading as an easier way to make better returns. The earnings are not verified or presented as typical, although the description includes a risk warning and affiliate-income disclosure.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker's earnings claim should be read with its qualifications, not as a promised result: he says "probably a week" and immediately acknowledges that it "seems like a Ponzi". The description expressly warns viewers about investment risk, tells them to use their own diligence, and discloses that links may benefit the creator. Those statements do not verify the earnings, but they weigh against reading the video as an assurance that viewers will earn the same return.

citations.quote: the copy training has earned me like way more Actually 11 percent probably a week which seems like a Ponzi
Please understand the risks of investing. All investing should be done with your own diligence.
Links may earn extra income to the creator to support the channel.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited $11 is presented as the speaker's net profit, not a promised payment to viewers. The weekly figure is likewise phrased as a personal estimate, with "probably" and an explicit comparison to a Ponzi. A description link invites participation, but the description also instructs viewers to assess investment risk themselves. The opening identifies promotion; it does not establish a guarantee.

citations.quote: They are open and we have a net profit of $ 11
the copy training has earned me like way more Actually 11 percent probably a week which seems like a Ponzi
Please understand the risks of investing. All investing should be done with your own diligence.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not erase the pitch. The speaker advocates copy trading for smaller traders, attributes an approximately weekly return to his own experience, and directs viewers to the description link to start. His qualification does not establish that the return is typical or verified; it leaves the promoted earnings claim unsubstantiated.

opening.argument: Judge, the video is framed as a review and guide, and the speaker compares trading bots with copy trading rather than presenting a single return as a fixed outcome. He says grid bots suit the short term while explaining his own preference for copy trading. The sampled screens show trading interfaces and leaderboards, which are consistent with demonstrating the features under discussion. That context supports treating the profit figures as examples being examined, not proof of what a viewer will receive.

citations.quote: BYBIT Grid Bot Review & Guide
grid bots are amazing for short term but what i prefer is long and fashioned rewards which is by copy training

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening rightly notes the earnings claim and invitation to use a link, but neither removes the review context. The speaker also discusses the possibility of liquidation in a bear market and challenges the idea that a one-day result will persist for a year. The leaderboard shows ranked entries, not evidence that every viewer can reproduce their figures.

Here the speaker says he prefers copy trading for long-term rewards, reports his own approximate weekly gain, and tells viewers to use the description link to get started. Showing an interface does not verify that his result is representative or offset that invitation.

opening.argument: Judge, the visible commercial offer is a link to trade crypto with an advertised bonus, accompanied by a disclosure that links may earn the creator income. The sampled screen shows a branded trading interface, and the speaker describes following other traders. Those facts establish a referral-style promotion of a trading service; they do not show a credential request, a downline payment arrangement, or a guaranteed payout. The promotional relationship deserves scrutiny, but it is not, by itself, evidence of those mechanisms.

Links may earn extra income to the creator to support the channel.
I just follow what other traders are doing and that's completely fine.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a bonus, claimed profits, and a link, but its cited material does not show the bonus being paid or a fixed return offered to everyone who follows the link. The speaker describes the $11 as his own net profit. An affiliate disclosure makes the commercial incentive visible; it does not validate the earnings, but it narrows what can be inferred about a concealed mechanism.
